es: Reconocer cómo el pasado y el pasado continuo suavizan una petición (I was wondering if…, I was hoping…) y ordenar peticiones de la más directa a la más distante.

teaching.en: I was wondering if you could spare a few minutes this afternoon, because I'd like to go over the report with you.
teaching.es: Me preguntaba si podrías dedicarme unos minutos esta tarde, porque me gustaría repasar el informe contigo.
teaching.explanationEs: I was wondering if + could: el pasado continuo crea distancia y la petición suena tentativa, aunque pidas algo para hoy.
segments: I was wondering if you could spare a few minutes this
afternoon, because I'd like to go over the report with you.
teaching.audioText: I was wondering if you could spare a few minutes this afternoon, because I'd like to go over the report with you.

teaching.en: Would you mind lending me your notes? I was hoping you could do me a favour before the exam on Friday.
teaching.es: ¿Te importaría prestarme tus apuntes? Esperaba que pudieras hacerme un favor antes del examen del viernes.
teaching.explanationEs: Would you mind va seguido de -ing; I was hoping suaviza igual que I was wondering y habla de ahora, no de ayer.
segments: Would you mind lending me your notes? I was hoping you
could do me a favour before the exam on Friday.
teaching.audioText: Would you mind lending me your notes? I was hoping you could do me a favour before the exam on Friday.

teaching.en: I hate to impose, but could I borrow your car, at your convenience, for a couple of hours this weekend?
teaching.es: No quisiera abusar, pero ¿podría pedirte prestado el coche, cuando te venga bien, un par de horas este fin de semana?
teaching.explanationEs: I hate to impose reconoce que pides un esfuerzo; at your convenience deja que el otro elija el momento.
segments: I hate to impose, but could I borrow your car,
at your convenience, for a couple of hours this weekend?
teaching.audioText: I hate to impose, but could I borrow your car, at your convenience, for a couple of hours this weekend?

teaching.en: A direct request like 'Lend me your pen' can sound abrupt, so speakers soften it by using could, might or a verb in the past.
teaching.es: Una petición directa como «Préstame tu bolígrafo» puede sonar brusca, así que los hablantes la suavizan con un tiempo pasado y un verbo modal.
teaching.explanationEs: Soften es rebajar la fuerza de la petición: could, might y el pasado continuo son los recursos habituales.
segments: A direct request like 'Lend me your pen' can sound abrupt, so speakers
soften it by using could, might or a verb in the past.
teaching.audioText: A direct request like 'Lend me your pen' can sound abrupt, so speakers soften it by using could, might or a verb in the past.

teaching.en: Her tone was tentative rather than demanding, which is why the request came across as polite instead of forceful.
teaching.es: Su tono era tentativo y no exigente, por eso la petición dio la impresión de ser cortés y no autoritaria.
teaching.explanationEs: Tentative describe lo que no se afirma con rotundidad; come across as indica la impresión que causa el mensaje.
segments: Her tone was tentative rather than demanding, which is why
the request came across as polite instead of forceful.
teaching.audioText: Her tone was tentative rather than demanding, which is why the request came across as polite instead of forceful.

teaching.en: With tact, you can make a request sound like a suggestion, so nobody feels pressured, even though you still want an answer.
teaching.es: Con tacto puedes hacer que una petición suene a sugerencia, de modo que nadie se sienta presionado, aunque sigas queriendo una respuesta.
teaching.explanationEs: Tact es la delicadeza de pedir sin presionar: dejas una salida al otro, pero la petición sigue en pie.
segments: With tact, you can make a request sound like a suggestion,
so nobody feels pressured, even though you still want an answer.
teaching.audioText: With tact, you can make a request sound like a suggestion, so nobody feels pressured, even though you still want an answer.

prompt.es: Lee el correo y elige qué efecto tiene «I was wondering if» en la petición.

choices.text: It makes the request tentative without moving it into the past.
It tells Mr Reed that she asked him the same thing before.
It turns the request into a polite order that he must follow.

feedback.es: El pasado continuo de wondering solo suaviza: la autora pide ahora, pero deja a Mr Reed libre para decir que no.

hint.es: Piensa en qué hace el tiempo verbal: crea distancia, no un pasado real.

origin.text: Dear Mr Reed, I hate to impose, but I was wondering if you could read my draft at your convenience. There is no rush at all.

prompt.es: Completa: «Odio abusar de ti, pero esperaba que me dedicaras unos minutos.»

feedback.es: Impose on someone significa abusar de su tiempo o de su amabilidad; I hate to impose prepara la petición que viene después.

hint.es: Es el verbo que se usa para molestar o abusar de la amabilidad de alguien.

origin.text: I hate to ___ on you, but I was hoping you could spare a few minutes before the meeting.

prompt.es: Ordena: «¿Te importaría prestarme tus apuntes cuando te venga bien?»

answer.text: Would you mind lending me your notes at your convenience

feedback.es: Would you mind exige -ing (lending), y at your convenience cierra la frase dejando elegir el momento al otro.

hint.es: Empieza por Would you mind y termina con la fórmula que cede el momento.

prompt.es: Escucha el pódcast y elige por qué la jefa usa «I was wondering if».

choices.text: To show her team that she has already asked for the figures.
To make her requests sound tentative, so nobody feels pressured.
To delay the figures until her team has more time to prepare.

feedback.es: La presentadora descubre que el pasado solo sirve para sonar tentativa: nadie se siente presionado y, curiosamente, el equipo trabaja más rápido.

origin.audio: In a podcast about good manners at work, the host explains that her manager never gives orders. Instead of saying, Send me the figures, she says, I was wondering if you could send me the figures when you get a chance. At first the host thought the past tense meant that her manager had already asked, but she soon realised that it was only a way of sounding tentative, so that nobody felt pressured. She adds that, curiously, the team works faster now, because the requests never feel like commands.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada fórmula con el efecto que tiene en la petición.

pairs.es: Deja elegir el momento al otro
Suaviza con un tiempo de distancia

feedback.es: Cada fórmula cumple una función distinta: reconocer el esfuerzo, ceder el momento, crear distancia con el pasado o, sin suavizar, dar una orden.

pairs.es: Deja elegir el momento al otro
Suaviza con un tiempo de distancia

prompt.es: Lee el correo. ¿Qué hace la autora con «do not feel you have to say yes»?

choices.text: She warns Sam that the deadline cannot be moved.
She complains that Sam usually refuses to help her.
She gives Sam a polite way out of the request.

feedback.es: La frase le ofrece a Sam una salida: pedir con tacto es reconocer que el otro puede negarse, sin reproche ni presión.

origin.text: Hi Sam, I was wondering whether you'd mind having a look at my proposal before Friday. I know it is a lot to ask, so please do not feel you have to say yes. If you are too busy, I will ask someone else.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de voz y elige qué da a entender Mia sobre su petición.

choices.text: She wants help soon but is ready to fit around Tom's schedule.
She has asked Tom before and is checking whether he forgot.
She is cancelling their meeting because Tom is too busy.

feedback.es: Mia pide ayuda para mañana, pero ofrece el jueves y deja a Tom decidir: quiere la ayuda sin imponer su calendario.

origin.audio: Hi Tom, it's Mia. I was wondering if you could spare ten minutes tomorrow, because I'm a bit stuck with the budget. I know you're busy with the launch, so if it's easier, we could do it on Thursday instead. Honestly, I'd hate to impose, so just tell me if it's a bad time. Anyway, let me know when you can.

prompt.es: Con el mismo mensaje, elige con qué propósito dice Mia «I'd hate to impose».

choices.text: To complain that Tom never finds time for her.
To let Tom refuse without feeling bad about it.
To apologise for phoning him during the launch.

feedback.es: I'd hate to impose prepara el «no» de Tom: Mia le deja claro que puede rechazar la petición sin que ella se ofenda.

origin.audio: Hi Tom, it's Mia. I was wondering if you could spare ten minutes tomorrow, because I'm a bit stuck with the budget. I know you're busy with the launch, so if it's easier, we could do it on Thursday instead. Honestly, I'd hate to impose, so just tell me if it's a bad time. Anyway, let me know when you can.

prompt.es: Completa: «Para suavizarla, muchos hablantes añaden un pasado y un modal.»

feedback.es: Soften es el verbo para rebajar la fuerza de una petición directa con could, might o un tiempo de distancia.

origin.text: A direct request can sound abrupt. To ___ it, many speakers add a past tense and a modal verb, so the request feels polite.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Esperaba que pudieras dedicarme unos minutos hoy.»

answer.text: I was hoping you might spare a few minutes today

feedback.es: I was hoping abre la petición con distancia, might la hace aún más tentativa y spare significa dedicar tiempo.

prompt.es: Lee el correo. ¿Qué deja entrever el autor sobre el plazo que le han dado?

choices.text: He accepts it gladly and sees nothing to discuss.
He thinks it unfair and refuses to begin the work.
He finds it tight but does not openly complain.

feedback.es: I was hoping we could discuss y my team is already very stretched insinúan que el plazo es ajustado, sin quejarse abiertamente.

origin.text: Dear Ms Lopez, thank you for your message. I'd be glad to help, but I was hoping we could discuss the deadline first, since my team is already very stretched. Would it be possible to meet on Wednesday?

prompt.es: Escucha la escena y elige qué tono tiene la petición del cliente.

choices.text: Polite and low-key, with no pressure on the waiter.
Nervous and shy, as if he expected a refusal.
Irritated and sarcastic, hiding a complaint about the music.

feedback.es: Excuse me, I was wondering y if you'd mind dan una petición cortés y tranquila; el cliente no presiona y la respuesta es amable.

origin.audio: At the café, a customer turns to the waiter and says, Excuse me, I was wondering if you'd mind turning the music down a little, because I'm trying to finish a call. The waiter nods and answers, Of course, I was about to do that myself. The customer smiles, looking relieved.

prompt.es: Completa: «¿Podría pedirte un favor? No es urgente.»

feedback.es: Ask someone a favour es la colocación habitual para pedir ayuda, y aclarar que no es urgente suaviza todavía más la petición.

origin.text: Could I ask you a ___? It is nothing urgent, so please take your time.

es: Usar verbos de estado y adjetivos en continuo para expresar conducta temporal o actitud (you're being silly, I'm loving it) y elegir entre simple y continuo según el matiz.

teaching.en: You're being silly today, which is out of character, because you are usually the most sensible person in the office.
teaching.es: Hoy estás haciendo el tonto, lo cual es impropio de ti, porque normalmente eres la persona más sensata de la oficina.
teaching.explanationEs: Be + being + adjetivo habla de la conducta de hoy; out of character señala que no es lo habitual en esa persona.
segments: You're being silly today, which is out of character, because
you are usually the most sensible person in the office.
teaching.audioText: You're being silly today, which is out of character, because you are usually the most sensible person in the office.

teaching.en: He is normally polite, but this week he's being rude to everyone, and we all hope it is only temporary.
teaching.es: Normalmente es educado, pero esta semana está siendo grosero con todos, y esperamos que sea solo algo temporal.
teaching.explanationEs: He's being rude es conducta de esta semana; He is rude sería su carácter.
segments: He is normally polite, but this week he's being rude
to everyone, and we all hope it is only temporary.
teaching.audioText: He is normally polite, but this week he's being rude to everyone, and we all hope it is only temporary.

teaching.en: Our teacher is strict by nature, yet lately she's being unusually strict about homework, and the whole class has noticed.
teaching.es: Nuestra profesora es estricta por naturaleza, pero últimamente está siendo especialmente estricta con los deberes, y toda la clase lo ha notado.
teaching.explanationEs: El continuo destaca un cambio: lately refuerza que es algo reciente, distinto de lo normal.
segments: Our teacher is strict by nature, yet lately she's being
unusually strict about homework, and the whole class has noticed.
teaching.audioText: Our teacher is strict by nature, yet lately she's being unusually strict about homework, and the whole class has noticed.

teaching.en: He's being stubborn about the plan, but for the time being nobody wants to argue with him.
teaching.es: Se está poniendo terco con el plan, pero de momento nadie quiere discutir con él.
teaching.explanationEs: For the time being indica algo provisional; combina bien con be being porque ambos hablan de lo temporal.

time being nobody wants to argue with him.
teaching.audioText: He's being stubborn about the plan, but for the time being nobody wants to argue with him.

teaching.en: You're being annoying, so please stop; I'm not saying you are an annoying person, only that your behaviour is irritating right now.
teaching.es: Estás siendo pesado, así que para, por favor; no digo que seas una persona pesada, solo que tu comportamiento resulta irritante ahora mismo.
teaching.explanationEs: Being annoying critica una conducta del momento; is annoying describiría a la persona.

teaching.en: I'm loving my new job lately, although my sister says I've been a bit moody since the move.
teaching.es: Últimamente me está encantando mi nuevo trabajo, aunque mi hermana dice que estoy algo de mal humor desde la mudanza.
teaching.explanationEs: I'm loving es un uso coloquial y enfático de love; moody describe un humor cambiante, no un rasgo fijo.

prompt.es: Lee el texto y elige la frase que describe la conducta de Tom esta semana.

choices.text: He is rude, which is typical of him.
He is being rude, which is out of character for him.
He has been rude since he was a child.

feedback.es: Tom suele ser amable: is being rude describe una conducta de esta semana, distinta de su forma de ser, y out of character lo confirma.

hint.es: Busca la forma que marca una conducta temporal y no un rasgo de carácter.

origin.text: Tom is normally the friendliest person on the team, but this week he has hardly said hello, and yesterday he answered a simple question with one word.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sueles ser generoso, ¿por qué hoy estás siendo tan terco con el precio?»

feedback.es: Con un adjetivo de conducta (stubborn), el continuo de be lleva being: are you being stubborn, para un comportamiento de hoy.

hint.es: Es la forma -ing de be que marca conducta temporal.

origin.text: You're usually so generous, so why are you ___ so stubborn about the price today?

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hoy está siendo muy generoso con su tiempo.»

answer.text: He is being very generous with his time today
accepted: He is being very generous with his time today
Today he is being very generous with his time

feedback.es: Be being + adjetivo da el matiz de conducta de hoy; very va delante del adjetivo y with his time dice en qué es generoso.

hint.es: Empieza por He is being y deja today para el final.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué da a entender la narradora sobre la conducta de su hermana.

choices.text: It shows that her real character has changed for good.
It was typical of her, because she is stubborn by nature.
It was unusual for her and probably linked to stress.

feedback.es: La narradora dice que fue out of character y temporal, y que su hermana está estresada: no es un cambio definitivo ni un rasgo fijo.

origin.audio: My sister has always been shy, so when she started talking loudly at dinner last night, we all looked at her. She was being very stubborn about where to go on holiday, and she even interrupted our father, which is completely out of character. Later she explained that she has been stressed lately and that her behaviour was only temporary. She promised that for the time being she would try to be more patient, and my father just laughed and said he was loving the new version of her.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase con el matiz que transmite.

pairs.es: Su conducta de hoy: suele no serlo
Reproche suave por una conducta concreta

feedback.es: Be + adjetivo describe el carácter; be being, la conducta del momento; I'm loving es un énfasis informal y You're being silly critica una acción concreta.

pairs.es: Su conducta de hoy: suele no serlo

prompt.es: Lee la nota. ¿Qué deduce la jefa sobre Carlos?

choices.text: That his attitude is temporary and probably has a cause.
That Carlos is a strict person who will never change.
That the new schedule was designed by Carlos himself.

feedback.es: He has never been like this before y something is worrying him sugieren que la severidad es temporal y tiene una causa, no un rasgo fijo.

origin.text: Note from the manager: 'Carlos is being very strict about the new schedule, and several people have mentioned it. He has never been like this before, so I suspect that something is worrying him.'

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje y elige qué actitud muestra el narrador hacia Leo.

choices.text: Angry and ready to end the friendship for good.
Confused but understanding, since he sees it as a passing stage.
Pleased, because he finds Leo's behaviour rather funny.

feedback.es: El narrador no entiende a Leo, pero atribuye su conducta a los exámenes y la llama temporal: confusión con comprensión, no enfado ni burla.

origin.audio: I honestly don't know what has got into Leo lately. He is usually so generous, but this week he's being stubborn about everything. On Monday he refused to share the taxi, and yesterday he wouldn't lend Mia a pen. I suppose it is only temporary, because his exams are coming, but it is certainly out of character.

prompt.es: Con el mismo audio, elige qué dice el narrador sobre cómo es Leo normalmente.

choices.text: He is usually stubborn about small matters.
He has always refused to share with others.
He is usually generous with his things.

feedback.es: El narrador contrasta He is usually so generous con la conducta terca de esta semana: lo habitual en Leo es la generosidad.

origin.audio: I honestly don't know what has got into Leo lately. He is usually so generous, but this week he's being stubborn about everything. On Monday he refused to share the taxi, and yesterday he wouldn't lend Mia a pen. I suppose it is only temporary, because his exams are coming, but it is certainly out of character.

prompt.es: Completa: «Gritar al camarero fue impropio de él, que es muy educado.»

feedback.es: Out of character es la colocación para algo impropio de una persona; aquí contrasta con su fama de educado.

origin.text: Shouting at the waiter was completely ___ of character for him, because he is usually the politest man I know.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Hoy está siendo inusualmente estricta con las nuevas normas.»

answer.text: She is being unusually strict about the new rules today
accepted: She is being unusually strict about the new rules today
Today she is being unusually strict about the new rules

feedback.es: She is being + unusually + adjetivo marca una conducta de hoy fuera de lo normal; about introduce aquello sobre lo que es estricta.

prompt.es: Lee el fragmento. ¿Qué sugiere la columnista sobre el enfado de su vecino?

choices.text: That the noise is a cover for another problem he has not mentioned.
That the noise really is impossible and must be reported.
That he has always complained about every single sound.

feedback.es: Normally a kind man y an excuse for something else sugieren que el ruido es un pretexto: la columnista sospecha de otro problema oculto.

origin.text: Columnist: 'My neighbour is being impossible this month. He is normally a kind man, yet now he complains about every noise. I'm trying to be patient, because I suspect that the noise is only an excuse for something else that is bothering him.'

prompt.es: Completa: «No recuerdo dónde vive, aunque lo conozco muy bien.»

feedback.es: Know es un verbo de estado y se queda en presente simple: I know him, nunca I am knowing him.

origin.text: I can't remember where he lives now, although I ___ him very well.

prompt.es: Escucha el reproche y elige qué distinción hace la hablante.

choices.text: She says his character is annoying every single day.
She criticises his behaviour today, not his character.
She regrets her own behaviour and says she is sorry.

feedback.es: La hablante separa la conducta de hoy (being annoying) del carácter (an annoying person): critica una acción, no a la persona.

origin.audio: You're being really annoying today, and I'm not saying you are an annoying person. I'm saying that your behaviour this afternoon is starting to bother me, so please stop.

title.es: Leer el tiempo en unas memorias

es: Interpretar qué tiempo verbal marca hábito, acción en curso o hecho anterior en un texto breve de memorias, leído y escuchado.

vocabulary.es: se dio cuenta, me di cuenta

teaching.en: In my memoir, I wrote that I used to live in a tiny flat in Lisbon, although in hindsight it was hardly big enough for two people.
teaching.es: En mis memorias escribí que solía vivir en un piso diminuto en Lisboa, aunque visto en retrospectiva apenas era lo bastante grande para dos personas.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to + verbo base cuenta un estado o hábito pasado que ya no existe; in hindsight añade la valoración de hoy.
segments: In my memoir, I wrote that I used to live in a tiny flat
in Lisbon, although in hindsight it was hardly big enough for two people.
teaching.audioText: In my memoir, I wrote that I used to live in a tiny flat in Lisbon, although in hindsight it was hardly big enough for two people.

teaching.en: Every morning I would walk to the river, and I remember vividly how the light changed; it became a habit I never questioned.
teaching.es: Cada mañana caminaba hasta el río, y recuerdo con nitidez cómo cambiaba la luz; se convirtió en una costumbre que nunca cuestioné.
teaching.explanationEs: Would + verbo base cuenta una acción repetida en el pasado; vividly describe lo claro que es el recuerdo.
segments: Every morning I would walk to the river, and I remember vividly
how the light changed; it became a habit I never questioned.
teaching.audioText: Every morning I would walk to the river, and I remember vividly how the light changed; it became a habit I never questioned.

teaching.en: I was walking home one evening when I realised that I had left my keys at the bakery, and by then it had started to rain.
teaching.es: Una tarde volvía andando a casa cuando me di cuenta de que había dejado las llaves en la panadería, y para entonces ya había empezado a llover.
teaching.explanationEs: Was walking es la escena en curso; had left es lo anterior; by then sitúa un hecho respecto a otro punto del pasado.
segments: I was walking home one evening when I realised that I had left
my keys at the bakery, and by then it had started to rain.
teaching.audioText: I was walking home one evening when I realised that I had left my keys at the bakery, and by then it had started to rain.

teaching.en: Gradually the streets stopped feeling foreign, although it took me almost a year to settle in properly.
teaching.es: Poco a poco las calles dejaron de parecerme extrañas, aunque me costó casi un año instalarme de verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Gradually marca un cambio lento; settle in es adaptarse a un lugar nuevo hasta sentirlo propio.
segments: Gradually the streets stopped feeling foreign, although it took
me almost a year to settle in properly.
teaching.audioText: Gradually the streets stopped feeling foreign, although it took me almost a year to settle in properly.

teaching.en: Looking back, I feel nostalgic about that year, even though I was working long hours and had already given up on the idea of a proper holiday.
teaching.es: Al mirar atrás, siento nostalgia de aquel año, aunque trabajaba muchas horas y ya había renunciado a la idea de unas vacaciones de verdad.
teaching.explanationEs: Was working presenta una etapa en curso; had given up es anterior; nostalgic expresa el sentimiento actual sobre ese pasado.
segments: Looking back, I feel nostalgic about that year, even though I was working long
hours and had already given up on the idea of a proper holiday.
teaching.audioText: Looking back, I feel nostalgic about that year, even though I was working long hours and had already given up on the idea of a proper holiday.

teaching.en: Her grandmother used to tell stories every night, and that habit shaped the way she wrote her memoir decades later.
teaching.es: Su abuela solía contar historias cada noche, y esa costumbre marcó la manera en que escribió sus memorias décadas después.
teaching.explanationEs: Used to + habit: una costumbre pasada; el pasado simple (shaped, wrote) cuenta lo que ocurrió como consecuencia.
segments: Her grandmother used to tell stories every night, and that
habit shaped the way she wrote her memoir decades later.
teaching.audioText: Her grandmother used to tell stories every night, and that habit shaped the way she wrote her memoir decades later.

prompt.es: Según el texto, ¿qué hacía el narrador cada mañana?

choices.text: He bought bread and ate it beside the river every day.
He baked bread at home before leaving for his work.
He woke to the smell of bread, then walked by the river.

feedback.es: Every morning + would wake up y used to walk describen costumbres: se despertaba con el olor a pan y paseaba junto al río antes de trabajar.

hint.es: Busca would y used to: marcan lo que hacía de forma repetida.

origin.text: When I first moved to Lisbon, I lived in a tiny flat above a bakery. Every morning I would wake up to the smell of bread, and I used to walk to the river before work. One evening I was walking home when it started to rain. By then I had already forgotten my umbrella, so I waited under a tree and watched the street empty. It took me months to settle in, but I remember that evening vividly, because it was the first time the city felt like mine.

prompt.es: Completa: «Me costó meses instalarme, pero recuerdo esa tarde con nitidez.»

feedback.es: Settle in es la colocación para adaptarse a un lugar nuevo hasta sentirlo propio; el verbo va en base tras to.

hint.es: Es el verbo que forma «adaptarse a un lugar» junto con in.

origin.text: The city felt strange at first. It took me months to ___ in, but I remember that evening vividly.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Para entonces ya había perdido las llaves.»

answer.text: By then I had already lost my keys

feedback.es: By then sitúa el hecho en un momento del pasado y had + participio marca que ocurrió antes de ese momento.

hint.es: Empieza por la marca temporal y usa had + participio.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué sugiere la narradora con «I had already guessed it was her».

choices.text: The call was so routine that she expected it.
Her grandmother had never phoned at that hour before.
She was angry about being interrupted while cooking.

feedback.es: Los domingos la llamada era una costumbre, por eso ya había adivinado quién era: el past perfect señala que lo supo antes de contestar.

origin.audio: Every Sunday my grandmother would call from the village. She used to ask the same three questions, and I used to give the same three answers. One day I was cooking when the phone rang, and by then I had already guessed it was her, because nobody else called at that hour.

prompt.es: Relaciona cada frase del relato con su perspectiva temporal.
